content.value_statement: Teams need clear charts from database questions without manual chart setup. This skill guides DBX Studio chart selection, SQL data queries, and generate_chart configuration.
actual_capabilities: Maps user intent to bar, line, pie, scatter, area, or histogram charts.
Provides generate_chart configuration fields for chart type, title, axes, data query, and grouping.
Supplies SQL patterns for top categories, time series, and proportion breakdowns.
Encourages descriptive titles and human-readable axis labels.
Recommends aggregation for large result sets and limits pie charts to seven slices.
limitations: Requires DBX Studio and its generate_chart tool to create the final chart.
Depends on accurate database schema names supplied by the user or project.
Does not validate query permissions, database credentials, or production safety.
Does not provide advanced statistical analysis beyond basic chart selection.

use_cases.title: Analyze revenue categories
use_cases.description: Create a bar chart that compares revenue across product categories using grouped SQL results.

use_cases.title: Track product trends
use_cases.description: Build a line chart that shows daily or monthly changes from time-based order data.

use_cases.title: Review operational breakdowns
use_cases.description: Use pie or histogram guidance to summarize status counts, distributions, or workload patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a bar chart of order count by status. Use a clear title and readable axis labels.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner chart request with a simple category comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Compare categories
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the top 10 product categories by revenue. Choose the best chart type and include the SQL query pattern.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request that needs grouping and ranking.

prompt_templates.title: Visualize trends
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a 30-day revenue trend chart from orders. Aggregate by day and explain the selected x_axis and y_axis names.
prompt_templates.scenario: Time series request that needs date aggregation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a complete chart plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a chart plan for comparing revenue by category over the last quarter, including chart type, query approach, grouping, title, and limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that needs a complete visualization plan.

output_examples.input: Show monthly revenue by product category.
output_examples.output: A bar chart plan with category on the x-axis, revenue on the y-axis, grouped by category, and a monthly revenue title.
A line chart recommendation that aggregates revenue by date and orders results chronologically.
A pie chart recommendation when status values are seven or fewer, with extra values grouped as Other.

best_practices: Aggregate large result sets before charting to improve performance and reduce sensitive row exposure.
Use chart titles that include the metric, grouping, and time period when relevant.
Keep axis labels readable for business users instead of exposing raw column names.
anti_patterns: Do not use pie charts for more than seven slices without grouping the remainder.
Do not chart raw row-level data when an aggregate view answers the question.
Do not choose scatter plots unless both axes use meaningful numeric values.

faq.question: What chart types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It documents bar, line, pie, scatter, area, and histogram chart choices for DBX Studio.

faq.question: Does it create SQL queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides query patterns for category counts, time series, and proportion breakdowns.

faq.question: Can it choose the right chart type?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps common user intent, such as trends or comparisons, to matching chart types.

faq.question: Does it work outside DBX Studio?
faq.answer: It is written for DBX Studio and assumes the generate_chart tool is available.

faq.question: How does it handle large result sets?
faq.answer: It recommends aggregation before charting to avoid raw row-level data.

faq.question: Can it validate database access?
faq.answer: No. Database permissions, credentials, and query safety must be handled by the host environment.
